$comment: LICENSE-PENDING — see docs/non_ratified/LICENSE_PENDING.md. loop-review.v1's wire shape is CLIENT-SIDE / STATIC-REGISTRY-COMPATIBLE (no field here presumes a hosted accounts/reviews database), but read LOOP_MARKETPLACE_CONTRACT.md §8 carefully before assuming this build-out stores any instance of it: 'Not built in this pass. Per the hard scope boundary above and 08_OPEN_QUESTIONS.md §E.1, structured reviews require a reviews database, which this build-out does not construct. This section is the interaction contract a future optional backend MUST follow if the owner turns reviews on; the static/Git registry (§11) carries no review mechanism of any kind.' This schema exists to give FB-RAT-MKT-006 a concrete wire shape per this work package's file-specific instruction and the traceability matrix's schema-target list — it is the contract a review record MUST have IF and WHEN reviews are ever turned on (the optional bounded backend §2 permits), not a claim that this repo persists, serves, or moderates any instance of this shape today. Flagged explicitly, not silently reframed as registry content, per this corpus's honesty convention.
title: LoopReview
description: loop-review.v1 — FB-RAT-MKT-006: 'Reviews separate usefulness, reliability, understandability, efficiency, and safety, plus a worked-for-me signal and free text.' Per LOOP_MARKETPLACE_CONTRACT.md §8, a review is release-specific (never a listing or a loopId alone) and carries a moderation state (§10). reviewerRef is pseudonymous by construction: this corpus has no accounts system anywhere (FB-RAT-INT-003, narrowly superseded only for deliberately published artifacts by FB-RAT-MKT-001) — a review's author identity is whatever pseudonymous identity the submission-by-pull-request process establishes (e.g. a GitHub handle on the PR that added this review to the optional backend's data, or to whatever mechanism eventually realizes §8), never a verified real-world identity, and this schema does not model one.

releaseIdentity.description: The release this review is about. MUST be a specific release, never a listing or a bare loopId (LOOP_MARKETPLACE_CONTRACT.md §8: 'declares: release identity (never a listing or a loopId alone — reviews are release-specific, §4)... Reviews MUST NOT silently migrate to a later release version merely because the loopId matches — a review of 1.2.0 says nothing about 1.3.0 unless the service explicitly carries it forward with that fact visible.').

freeText.description: Free-text review body. MAY be an empty string (a rating-only review with no prose) — the field itself is required so a decoder never has to distinguish 'no free text field' from 'empty free text', but empty content is permitted. Same publication-time LOOP-PKG-006 (invisible-Unicode) / LOOP-PKG-008 (prompt-risk) scanning that applies to a listing's description (loop-listing.schema.json) applies here — a review body is exactly as model/human-readable as a listing, and is an equally plausible prompt-injection target (see this schema's adversarial/ fixtures).

moderationState.description: Subset of LOOP_MARKETPLACE_CONTRACT.md §10's six-state moderation table (PENDING/PUBLISHED/LIMITED/DELISTED/TAKEDOWN) — KEY_REVOKED is deliberately excluded here because §10 states it 'applies to a publisher's key, not to one release's editorial state' (and a review is neither a release nor a key); a revoked publisher key does not, on its own, change any single review's moderationState. Transitions follow the same from-state/event/to-state table §10 defines for marketplace content generally; not re-derived here.

verifiedInstallRef.description: Optional reference to a verified-install record (LOOP_MARKETPLACE_CONTRACT.md §8: 'optional verified-install/verified-run references'). Untyped reference string (not an inline object) because the full shape of an install/run verification receipt is owned by LOOP_RESULT_SHARING_CONTRACT.md and LOOP_IMPORT_ACTIVATION_CONTRACT.md respectively — not redefined here.

verifiedRunRef.description: Optional reference to a verified-run record, same rationale as verifiedInstallRef — LOOP_RESULT_SHARING_CONTRACT.md owns the shared-result-receipt shape this would point at.

createdAtUtc.description: UTC instant this review was authored.

ReviewRatings.description: The five separate rating dimensions FB-RAT-MKT-006 names explicitly, each independently scored — never collapsed into one aggregate star rating (that collapse is exactly what 'separate' rules out). NOTE: neither FB-RAT-MKT-006's decision text nor any other ratified document in this corpus fixes a numeric scale for these ratings — a 1-5 integer scale is this schema's own authoring choice (documented at RatingScale below), not a ratified decision. Flagged for the Amendments-phase agent if the owner wants a different scale (e.g. 1-10, or a non-numeric enum) fixed instead.

RatingScale.description: 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest) integer scale. Schema-authoring choice, not a ratified numeric range — see ReviewRatings' description.

pseudonymousId.description: Whatever pseudonymous identity the submission-by-pull-request process establishes for this review (e.g. the GitHub handle that opened the PR carrying it) — NOT a real-world verified identity. This corpus has no accounts system for the marketplace's static/Git registry (§11); reviews specifically are not even built by this pass (§8, 'Not built in this pass') — this field documents the constraint a future optional backend MUST honor if it ever assigns review authorship, rather than assuming a real user-account system exists.

submissionRef.description: Optional pointer establishing pseudonymousId's provenance (e.g. a PR URL or number) — mirrors §11's 'the PR and its review are the audit trail' pattern for whichever mechanism eventually carries reviews.
